title: Verlintas/NOIR
body:
手机隐私审计：用 adb 扫出 Android 应用的权限、上报端点与数据流向，并给出可回滚的处置。Desktop Android leak audit: permissions, endpoints, data flows, reversible fixes.

README 節錄：``` ███╗ ██╗ ██████╗ ██╗██████╗ ████╗ ██║██╔═══██╗██║██╔══██╗ ██╔██╗ ██║██║ ██║██║██████╔╝ ██║╚██╗██║██║ ██║██║██╔══██╗ ██║ ╚████║╚██████╔╝██║██║ ██║ ╚═╝ ╚═══╝ ╚═════╝ ╚═╝╚═╝ ╚═╝ ``` # NOIR **把「这台手机到底能泄露什么」变成一份可复现的报告。** NOIR 是一个跑在电脑上的审计工具，通过 `adb` 读取已连接 Android 设备的应用清单、权限和 APK 里的网络端点，给出分类、风险评分和可执行的处置建议。它也可以在需要时调用 `jadx` 对单个应用做反编译和关键字检索。 > 定位：**审计与自我防护**。面向自己的设备、自己的应用、已授权的安全研究。 **官网 / Website:** https://verlintas.dev/noir/ · 中文 **AtomGit 镜像 / Mirror:** https://atomgit.com/Verlintas/NOIR --- ## 它做什么 1. **盘点**：列出所有「有网络权限 + 敏感权限」的应用，以及它们各自拿到了什么。 2. **抽取端点**：在设备端用 `unzip + strings` 从每个 APK 的 dex 里提取 URL，只回传几 KB，不把整包拉回电脑。 3. **分类与打分**：按包名和域名识别厂商（Xiaomi / Google / 腾讯 / 高德 …）与类别（遥测、广告、定位、输入法 …），结合权限和上报端点计算风险分。 4. **数据关联**：把权限翻译成"能拿到什么数据"（位置/通讯录/短信/通话/麦克风/相机/屏幕/应用列表/设备标识/文件/日历/账号），再和上报域名配对，得出"哪类数据可能流向哪里"。 5. **共享 UID**：识别 `android.uid.system` 这类共享用户，列出哪些包实际上共享同一套权限并集。 6. **清单层**：解析 `AndroidManifest.xml` 二进制 AXML，找出没有权限保护的导出组件、明文流量、备份、debuggable、targetSdk。 4. **给建议**：区分「可安全自动执行」「需人工确认」「不建议动」，并为每条动作生成回滚命令。 5. **必要时深挖**：`deep` 会把单个 APK 拉到本地，用 `jadx` 反编译后检索 `Runtime.exec`、`setApplicationEnabledSetting`、`DexClassLoader`、`MediaProjection` 等高风险调用。 ## 它不做什么 - 不联网、不上传任何数据、不需要账号。 - 不修改系统分区，不需要 root。 - 不会自动卸载任何东西，除非你显式加 `--aggressive`。 --- ## 第一次运行 ```bash noir ``` 不带参数会进入向导： 1. 检查 `adb`，没有就**问你要不要自动下载**（`~/.noir/tools`） 2. 检查设备，没有就打印**开发者模式 / USB 调试的开通步骤

README 節錄：# FlashProve Version 0.16.0 · A research artifact: not maintained, not accepting contributions. · Apache 2.0 ## What it is FlashProve lets an AI provider prove which model answered a request, without revealing the model's weights. - **Commit.** The provider publishes a commitment ID, which binds it to one set of weights. The weights themselves stay secret: every published value that depends on them is masked, except a declared list. - **Prove.** For each reply, the provider's GPU produces a proof that the reply is the committed model's output. - **Verify.** Anyone can check the proof on an ordinary CPU in seconds with `cp_verify`, without the weights. ## What model it runs FlashProve runs Llama 4 Maverick at full size, with a 1,024-token context window, on a single NVIDIA H100. The prover reaches about 110 tokens/second of prefill at 24 requests per batch (Performance). ## What is proved The protocol's soundness is proved in Lean 4. A provider that tries to pass off output that is not the committed model's is caught, except with probability about q/2^124 + 2^-101 after q hash queries. lean/THEOREM.md has the theorem and how to check it. ## Built to be run by an agent Building FlashProve, running it and checking its output take long builds and many exact comparisons. body: I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. Are you sticking with the default CLIs or IDE integrations, or using alternatives like OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Muse Code, or custom-built harnesses? - What made you switch harnesses (if you switched)? 4) Are you using any agent orchestration or swarm tools? - For example, Munder Difflin, Gas Town, Ruflo, or something custom. 5) Are you using broader agent platforms like OpenClaw / Hermes Agent / Grok bot / Dots / Muse? - If you are using them, what are your main use cases? ----- I know my workflow has differed significantly from a year ago, and so it would be interesting to capture a snapshot today of what people are using and why. Value your Steam stash in the terminal and print it as a share card: per game, per market, what sold and what sits. One Windows portable build, no account.

README 節錄： ```text $ stashcard paste a profile -> pick a card -> get a PNG worth posting ``` **Stashcard** values a Steam account and its inventories (CS2, Dota 2, TF2, Rust, Steam community items or any custom app) from your terminal, prices them on Steam and on the big cash marketplaces, and prints the result as a shareable card: a report card, a game card, an inventory picture, a thermal receipt, a marketplace comparison, or a then-vs-now / A-vs-B diff. Every number carries its venue and window. `LOWEST` is the floor listing right now. `AVG` is the mean of real sales over a window you pick. Steam money is wallet funds; everything else is cash, and the two are never mixed silently. When a source has nothing, Stashcard falls back and says so on the row, in the totals and in the card footer. Nothing unpriced is ever counted as zero. Free and open source. No accounts, no paid APIs, no telemetry. > [!TIP] > **Run Stashcard on your home PC. Windows is the recommended setup.** Steam rate-limits datacenter, > VPS and cloud IPs heavily, so live scans from a server are unreliable. On a server only the demo and > cached data work reliably. title: joeblau/subvox
body: README 節錄：# Subvox A macOS prototype that tests whether AirPods Pro head-motion data (`CMHeadphoneMotionManager`) carries enough information to turn **silently mouthed words into text**. It doesn't use a language model. It's a small-vocabulary template recognizer plus a statistical test that tells you whether the signal is real. ## Build & run ```sh brew install xcodegen # once xcodegen generate open Subvox.xcodeproj # ⌘R ``` Or from the command line: ```sh xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build -allowProvisioningUpdates build open build/Build/Products/Debug/Subvox.app xcodebuild -project Subvox.xcodeproj -scheme Subvox -derivedDataPath build test ``` Requires macOS 14+, AirPods Pro or another headphone that supports head tracking, connected as the Mac's audio output. On first launch, grant **Motion**. The mic and speech prompts only appear when you start the mic. ## Screens | Screen | What it does | |---|---| | **Sensors** | Live plots of user acceleration, rotation rate and attitude, the measured sample rate, a mic input picker and level meter, and a recorder for experiment sessions. | | **Train** | Pick a word, hold **Space**, mouth it, release. Each take is stored as a template. **Evaluate** runs leave-one-out classification and a 500× label-permutation test, then shows accuracy against chance, a p-value and a confusion matrix. The feature checkboxes (acceleration / rotation / attitude) let you test which channels carry the signal. |
